title: ML-MT121-MtSignalContract

scope.summary:
GOAL: Define hsk.mt_signal@1 — the single mechanical completion-signal contract every MT-dispatched worker MUST emit as its structured exit. This is the mechanism that replaces polling (polling is FORBIDDEN by operator rule): the worker's final structured output IS the signal; Handshake parses it, advances the MT run, and notifies the orchestrator. The schema is handed to workers at launch as their required output shape via the structured-exit transports: MT-027 Claude `--json-schema`, MT-046 Codex `--output-schema`, and final-message parse on the ACP lane.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: One new backend module src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/mt_signal.rs (Rust types + serde + validation + exported JSON Schema document + typed parse errors), wired into swarm_orchestration/mod.rs, plus unit tests. No GUI, no routes, no PG in this MT.

DETAILED SPEC — hsk.mt_signal@1 fields:
- schema_id: string, MUST equal "hsk.mt_signal@1" (versioning anchor; parser rejects any other value with a typed error, so a v2 can be introduced without silent misparse).
- signal: enum, exactly one of: MT_IMPLEMENTED | READY_FOR_VALIDATION | BLOCKED | NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF | FAILED | PARTIAL_WITH_DISCLOSURE.
- wp_id: non-empty string (echo of the dispatched work packet id).
- mt_id: non-empty string matching ^MT-\d+$ (echo of the dispatched microtask id).
- session_id: non-empty string (the worker's Handshake session id, injected at launch by the dispatcher MT-122; used for attribution and receipt correlation).
- evidence: array of objects { command: string, exit_code: integer, summary: string } — one entry per executed proof target from the MT contract's scope.proof_targets. REQUIRED non-empty when signal is MT_IMPLEMENTED or READY_FOR_VALIDATION.
- changed_paths: array of strings (repo-relative paths the worker touched; empty array allowed for BLOCKED/FAILED).
- blocker: nullable object { kind: enum MISSING_DEPENDENCY | MANAGED_RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE | SCOPE_CONFLICT | TOOL_FAILURE | PERMISSION_DENIED | OTHER_DISCLOSED, detail: non-empty string }. REQUIRED non-null when signal is BLOCKED or NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF; MUST be null when signal is MT_IMPLEMENTED or READY_FOR_VALIDATION.
- notes: nullable string. REQUIRED non-empty when signal is PARTIAL_WITH_DISCLOSURE (the disclosure itself).

RUST TYPES (src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/mt_signal.rs):
- pub enum MtSignalKind { MtImplemented, ReadyForValidation, Blocked, NeedsManagedResourceProof, Failed, PartialWithDisclosure } with serde rename to the SCREAMING_SNAKE wire names above.
- pub struct MtSignal { schema_id, signal: MtSignalKind, wp_id, mt_id, session_id, evidence: Vec<MtSignalEvidence>, changed_paths: Vec<String>, blocker: Option<MtSignalBlocker>, notes: Option<String> }.
- pub struct MtSignalEvidence { command: String, exit_code: i32, summary: String }.
- pub struct MtSignalBlocker { kind: MtSignalBlockerKind, detail: String } and pub enum MtSignalBlockerKind (six kinds above).
- pub enum SignalParseFailure (thiserror): UnsupportedSchema { found: String }, MalformedJson { reason: String, raw_excerpt: String }, UnknownSignalKind { found: String }, CrossFieldViolation { rule: String } — malformed or rule-violating signals ALWAYS surface as this typed error carrying a bounded raw excerpt (first 512 chars) for diagnostics; NEVER a silent None/default.
- pub fn parse_mt_signal(raw: &str) -> Result<MtSignal, SignalParseFailure> — parses, checks schema_id, then runs validate_mt_signal.
- pub fn validate_mt_signal(sig: &MtSignal) -> Result<(), SignalParseFailure> — enforces the cross-field rules (evidence/blocker/notes requirements per signal kind, id shape rules).
- pub fn mt_signal_json_schema() -> serde_json::Value — the canonical JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) document handed verbatim to workers as the --json-schema / --output-schema payload; MUST declare required fields, the closed signal enum, and additionalProperties true at the top level (forward-compat: v1 consumers tolerate unknown EXTRA fields but reject unknown signal kinds and wrong schema_id).

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read swarm_orchestration/mod.rs and events.rs in the product worktree to match existing module conventions (thiserror errors, serde derives, SCREAMING_SNAKE wire enums).
2. Create mt_signal.rs with the types, parse/validate functions, and mt_signal_json_schema() exactly as specced above.
3. Wire `pub mod mt_signal;` into swarm_orchestration/mod.rs with re-exports matching the module's existing export style.
4. Unit tests (same file or swarm_orchestration/tests.rs per crate convention): happy-path parse for each of the six signal kinds; schema_id "hsk.mt_signal@2" -> UnsupportedSchema; garbage JSON -> MalformedJson with raw excerpt; signal READY_FOR_VALIDATION with empty evidence -> CrossFieldViolation; signal BLOCKED with null blocker -> CrossFieldViolation; unknown extra top-level field -> parses OK; unknown signal kind -> UnknownSignalKind; round-trip serialize/deserialize equality; mt_signal_json_schema() output itself parses as JSON and contains all six enum values.
5. Run proof targets; record measured output.
forbidden_paths: app/src/** (legacy React; GUI surface exception exists only on the board MT MT-125)
.GOV/** (the product READS MT contracts; it never writes .GOV)
.GOV/tools/handshake-acp-bridge/** (repo-gov broker stays as-is; product takeover is a separate cutover)
acceptance_criteria: mt_signal.rs exists, is wired into swarm_orchestration/mod.rs, and `cargo build -p handshake_core` is green.
All six signal kinds parse and round-trip; wire names are exactly MT_IMPLEMENTED, READY_FOR_VALIDATION, BLOCKED, NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF, FAILED, PARTIAL_WITH_DISCLOSURE.

Cross-field validation enforced: READY_FOR_VALIDATION/MT_IMPLEMENTED require non-empty evidence and null blocker; BLOCKED/NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF require a typed non-null blocker; PARTIAL_WITH_DISCLOSURE requires non-empty notes.
Malformed input NEVER degrades silently: every failure path returns a typed SignalParseFailure variant carrying a reason and a bounded raw excerpt.
Wrong schema_id is rejected with UnsupportedSchema (versioning gate proven by test).

mt_signal_json_schema() returns a valid JSON document declaring the closed signal enum and required fields, suitable to hand to MT-027 (--json-schema), MT-046 (--output-schema), and the ACP final-message parser.
Unknown extra top-level fields are tolerated (forward-compat) while unknown signal kinds are rejected.
expected_tests: parse happy path for all six MtSignalKind values
MalformedJson with raw excerpt on garbage input
CrossFieldViolation: empty evidence on READY_FOR_VALIDATION; null blocker on BLOCKED; empty notes on PARTIAL_WITH_DISCLOSURE
UnknownSignalKind rejection; unknown extra field tolerance
implementation_notes: This schema is the worker-facing half of the no-polling contract: the worker emits it ONCE as structured exit; MT-123 consumes it as the state-machine input; MT-122 embeds mt_signal_json_schema() in the launch payload. Keep it dependency-light (serde + thiserror only) so transports can reuse it without pulling coordinator internals.

Do NOT hand-write the JSON Schema string by concatenation; build it as a serde_json::json! literal (or schemars if already a workspace dep — check Cargo.toml first, do not add new deps without need) so tests can assert structure, not string equality.

The bounded raw excerpt in SignalParseFailure exists because FR/ledger recording (MT-123/MT-161) must be able to show WHAT the worker actually emitted; truncate at a fixed 512-char constant to keep events bounded.

Blocker kinds mirror the typed-blocker discipline already used in governance (NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF precedent in WP-KERNEL-012 MT lifecycle): a worker that cannot prove against a managed resource signals NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF with kind MANAGED_RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE rather than fabricating PASS language.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Headless schema/types MT; operator-visible MT-run state ships on the board MT MT-125.

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Internal contract module; the UserManual entry for the MT dispatch loop lands with MT-126 (end-to-end behavior) and MT-125 (operator surface).

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.obligation: SignalParseFailure variants expose machine-readable reason + bounded raw excerpt for no-context diagnosis.
Parse failures are constructed so MT-123 can record them to FR/ledger verbatim; no failure path returns an untyped error string.
Deferred to MT-125 (board shows last signal + parse-failure state); recorded here as the consuming surface.

risk_if_missed: No mechanical completion signal exists; workers can only be polled or free-text-parsed, which the operator has forbidden — the entire ML dispatch lifecycle (MT-122..126) is blocked.

risks: RISK-1: A worker emits plausible free text instead of the schema and a lenient parser 'best-efforts' it into a success signal — fabricated completion enters the lifecycle.
RISK-2: Schema evolution breaks silently — a future v2 field change is parsed by v1 consumers as defaults, mis-advancing runs.
RISK-3: A worker signals READY_FOR_VALIDATION with empty evidence (no proof targets actually run), laundering an unproven claim into validation handoff.
RISK-4: Unbounded raw payload embedded in errors/events lets a malicious or broken worker bloat the FR/ledger (resource abuse via error path).
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): parse_mt_signal is strict — schema_id gate + closed signal enum + typed failures; there is no lenient/heuristic fallback path in the codebase.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): schema_id equality check with UnsupportedSchema rejection proven by test; unknown EXTRA fields tolerated, unknown signal kinds rejected — explicit, tested version posture.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): cross-field rule 'success signals require non-empty evidence' enforced in validate_mt_signal and covered by a negative test.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): raw excerpt truncated at a fixed 512-char constant; asserted by test.

research_provenance.source: WP-017 stub research basis (2026-07-21 dossiers: Claude --json-schema structured exit, Codex --output-schema, ACP final-message parse; Anthropic multi-agent worker prompts carry objective/output-format/boundaries) + verified product code: swarm_orchestration/{mod,events,coordinator}.rs conventions in wtc-multi-model-orchestration-v1.
corrections: Signal vocabulary extends the governance typed-blocker precedent (NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF / BLOCKED / PARTIAL_WITH_DISCLOSURE seen in WP-KERNEL-012 MT lifecycle) rather than inventing a new blocker taxonomy.
Polling is forbidden by operator rule; the structured exit IS the completion mechanism — schema designed to be self-sufficient for run advancement without any status query.
